Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. An external scalar datum consists of a spin-zero species assigned a mass $m>0$ and elastic two-particle threshold $s=4m^2$. This is a mathematical input package; it does not construct a one-particle scattering state or a scattering matrix. For real on-shell momenta $p_1,p_2$ incoming and $p_3,p_4$ outgoing, with $p_j^2=-m^2$ and $p_1+p_2=p_3+p_4$, define

$$s=-(p_1+p_2)^2,\qquad t=-(p_1-p_3)^2,\qquad u=-(p_1-p_4)^2.$$

Then $s+t+u=4m^2$. The forward slice is the complex-valued function $A(s)=\mathcal A(s,0,4m^2-s)$ obtained by analytically continuing the identical-scalar $2\to2$ amplitude to $t=0$. The crossing action on this slice is $s\mapsto4m^2-s$, which exchanges $s$ and $u$. Assume $A(s)=A(4m^2-s)$ wherever both sides are defined.

For context, when a full $t$-dependent amplitude is supplied, use the partial-wave normalization

$$\mathcal A(s,t,u)=16\pi\sqrt{\frac{s}{s-4m^2}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}(2\ell+1)P_\ell\!\left(1+\frac{2t}{s-4m^2}\right)a_\ell(s),\qquad P_\ell(1)=1,$$

where $\ell$ is a nonnegative integer and $P_\ell$ is the Legendre polynomial. The forward result below uses only the optical-theorem sign $\operatorname{Im}A(s+i0)\ge0$ for $s>4m^2$; a full partial-wave realization is not inferred from this definition. In the displayed normalization, this sign follows when the forward partial-wave sum converges and the supplied partial waves obey $\operatorname{Im}a_\ell(s)\ge|a_\ell(s)|^2\ge0$.

Put $\nu_0=2m^2$ and $v=s-2m^2$, so $u-2m^2=-v$. Choose finitely many real numbers $p_j\in(0,4m^2)\setminus\{2m^2\}$ and real residues $r_j$, and set

$$P(s)=\sum_j\left(\frac{r_j}{s-p_j}+\frac{r_j}{4m^2-p_j-s}\right).$$

Each summand pair is the real simple-pole principal part at $s=p_j$ and its $s\leftrightarrow u$ crossing partner; hence $P(4m^2-s)=P(s)$. These poles lie off the two-particle cuts. Define the pole-subtracted forward function $B(v)=A(2m^2+v)-P(2m^2+v)$. Assume $B$ is holomorphic on

$$\Omega_{\nu_0}=\mathbb C\setminus\bigl((-\infty,-\nu_0]\cup[\nu_0,\infty)\bigr),$$

real analytic there, meaning $B(\overline v)=\overline{B(v)}$, and has finite upper and lower boundary values on both cuts except at their endpoints. Here the two-particle gap is the open interval $(-\nu_0,\nu_0)$ in the $v$ variable; no massless pole or cut reaches the forward point $t=0$.

Require additionally that $B$ extends continuously from each open half-plane onto every compact segment of either real cut bank avoiding $\pm\nu_0$. This is an extra admissibility assumption on the supplied data, not a consequence of finite pointwise boundary values or a claim about every quantum field theory. 

Assume the exact high-energy condition $B(w)=o(|w|^2)$ uniformly as $|w|\to\infty$ in the closed upper half-plane, including upper cut-bank limits. In particular this holds on the large upper semicircles after any fixed bounded horizontal translation. For $\nu\ge\nu_0$, define the absorptive density $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}B(\nu+i0)$. Require $\rho$ to be nonnegative and Riemann integrable on every compact subinterval of $[\nu_0,\infty)$, and require $\int_{\nu_0}^{\infty}\rho(\nu)\nu^{-3}\,d\nu$ to converge as a finite improper Riemann integral. For every real $v$ with $|v|<\nu_0$, require the integrals along both sides of the two cuts of $[B(x)-B(0)]/[x^2(x-v)]$, with boundary values taken from the upper and lower half-planes, to exist as finite improper Riemann limits. Require also that the small endpoint arcs at $\pm\nu_0$ for this integrand vanish in the contour limit. Since $P$ is real off its poles, $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}A(2m^2+\nu+i0)$ for $\nu>\nu_0$ on the right cut.

The normalized forward Taylor coefficients are $c_n=B^{(2n)}(0)/(2n)!$ for integers $n\ge1$. They have units $(\text{mass})^{-4n}$; $\nu_0$ has units $(\text{mass})^2$. No sign is assigned here to a generic off-shell Lagrangian coefficient.

A local operator in this finite-order data is an element of $P_{r,q,D}$ evaluated at $x$ on the $r$-jet of the fields. A scalar operator invariant under the declared symmetries is an element of $V_{r,q,D}=P_{r,q,D}^{G}$. Engineering dimension means this assigned mass weight; it is not a statement about an observed quantity. In four dimensions a term with operator $\mathcal O_D$ has the convention $C\mathcal O_D/\Lambda^{D-4}$, where $\Lambda$ has mass dimension one and $C$ is dimensionless.

derivations.claim: Identify the shared positive scalar mass and translate the two-particle threshold to the positive forward-variable cut endpoint.
Check the field, derivative, polynomial-degree, invariant-scalar, and Lagrangian dimensions for the chosen finite-jet operator.
Verify termwise that the paired pole subtraction is crossing even, so subtracting it preserves the supplied forward crossing relation.

Let $\phi\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ be a real, Grassmann-even (commuting) scalar field of engineering dimension one, with a stable one-particle state of pole mass $m>0$; here stable means an isolated real mass pole with zero decay width. Stability and the existence of this state are physical input data; no construction of a state is asserted. An effective field theory (EFT) here is the selected local low-energy representative organized in powers of its cutoff; its exact amplitude is separate supplied model data. For the finite-jet local-operator convention, use the complexification for the finite-jet algebra and impose the usual reality condition on $\phi$. Take one field species, maximum jet order $r=1$, polynomial degree at most $q=4$, weight $D=8$, trivial internal group, and the standard Lorentz tensor action with contractions formed using $\eta$. The real operator $\mathcal O_8=(\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi)^2$ is then a local scalar of engineering dimension eight. Its coefficient in a chosen local representative is written

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EFT}}=-\frac12\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi-\frac12m^2\phi^2+\frac{C_8(\mu_*)}{\Lambda^4}\mathcal O_8+\cdots,$$

where $\Lambda>2m$ is the positive energy cutoff of the EFT description, $0<\mu_*<\Lambda$ is the chosen scale at which the coefficient and matching identity are specified, and $C_8(\mu_*)\in\mathbb R$ is dimensionless in the fixed coefficient convention and local representative. No basis-independence under field redefinitions, equations of motion, or integration by parts is asserted for $C_8$ itself.

The amplitude data consist of an identical-scalar $2\to2$ amplitude $\mathcal A(s,t,u)$ and real on-shell momenta $p_j$ with $p_j^2=-m^2$, $p_1+p_2=p_3+p_4$, and

$$s=-(p_1+p_2)^2,\qquad t=-(p_1-p_3)^2,\qquad u=-(p_1-p_4)^2,\qquad s+t+u=4m^2.$$

The forward slice is $A(s)=\mathcal A(s,0,4m^2-s)$ and assume $A(s)=A(4m^2-s)$ wherever both sides are defined. When the full $t$-dependent amplitude is supplied, use the partial-wave normalization

$$\mathcal A(s,t,u)=16\pi\sqrt{\frac{s}{s-4m^2}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}(2\ell+1)P_\ell\!\left(1+\frac{2t}{s-4m^2}\right)a_\ell(s),\qquad P_\ell(1)=1.$$

Here $\ell=0,1,2,\ldots$, $P_\ell$ is the Legendre polynomial, and $a_\ell(s)$ is the partial-wave coefficient. The formula is a normalization convention when a full amplitude is supplied; it does not assert convergence or unitarity by itself.

The $S$-matrix convention is $S=1+i(2\pi)^4\delta^4(p_{\mathrm{out}}-p_{\mathrm{in}})\mathcal A+\cdots$. The channel adopts the forward optical-theorem input $\operatorname{Im}A(s+i0)\ge0$ for $s>4m^2$ in this normalization. This sign is an assumption on the supplied amplitude data, not a deduction from the EFT truncation.

Put $\nu_0=2m^2$ and $v=s-2m^2$, so $u-2m^2=-v$. Let the specified finite list contain every isolated variable simple pole in the subthreshold interval, with real locations $p_j\in(0,4m^2)\setminus\{2m^2\}$ and real residues $r_j$. For the dimensionless amplitude convention above, $r_j$ has mass dimension two. Define the crossing-symmetric pole subtraction

$$P(s)=\sum_j\left(\frac{r_j}{s-p_j}+\frac{r_j}{4m^2-p_j-s}\right),\qquad B(v)=A(2m^2+v)-P(2m^2+v).$$

The exact amplitude data are required to be crossing even and real analytic, with $B(-v)=B(v)$, $B(\overline v)=\overline{B(v)}$, and $B$ holomorphic on

$$\Omega_{\nu_0}=\mathbb C\setminus\bigl(( -\infty,-\nu_0]\cup[\nu_0,\infty)\bigr).$$

There is no massless pole or cut at the forward point $t=0$. Require finite upper and lower cut-boundary values except at $\pm\nu_0$. Also require $B$ to extend continuously from each open half-plane onto every compact segment of either real cut bank avoiding $\pm\nu_0$. This is an extra admissibility assumption on the supplied data, not a consequence of finite pointwise boundary values or a claim about every quantum field theory. Require the uniform high-energy condition $B(w)=o(|w|^2)$ as $|w|\to\infty$ in the closed upper half-plane including upper cut-bank limits, and vanishing endpoint arcs for the cut integrals. For $\nu>\nu_0$, let $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}B(\nu+i0)$ and assign $\rho(\nu_0)=0$ by convention, without asserting a threshold boundary limit; changing this one endpoint value changes no Riemann integral; require $\rho\ge0$, local Riemann integrability on every compact subinterval of $[\nu_0,\infty)$, and finite convergence of $\int_{\nu_0}^{\infty}\rho(\nu)\nu^{-3}\,d\nu$. For every real $|v|<\nu_0$, the upper- and lower-bank integrals of $[B(x)-B(0)]/[x^2(x-v)]$ are required to exist as finite improper Riemann limits. The positive gap $m>0$ and these analytic and spectral assumptions are IR and UV input conditions; they are not derived from a finite regulator.

Define the first nonconstant even forward coefficient by $c_1=B''(0)/2!$, of mass dimension $-4$. Exact matching at $\mu_*$ is a supplied datum of the form

$$c_1=\frac{4C_8(\mu_*)}{\Lambda^4}+\Delta_{\mathrm{match}},$$

where $\Delta_{\mathrm{match}}\in\mathbb R$ has mass dimension $-4$ and contains every other contribution to this exact $v^2$ coefficient, including other operators, loops, and matching or truncation effects. The identity is an assumption to be checked for a selected model, not a conclusion of this definition. Setting $\Delta_{\mathrm{match}}=0$ is an additional exact retained-order matching condition; power counting alone does not set it to zero.

Let $U_D\subset V_D$ be the subspace of degree-exactly-four scalar polynomials whose indices are contracted using $\eta$ only, and let $Q_D^{(4)}$ be its image in $\mathcal Q_D$. Thus $Q_D^{(4)}=U_D/(U_D\cap R_D)$; operators outside this image are not assigned a contact map.

Require the following certificate for the actual declared relations: every $H\in U_D\cap R_D$ is a finite sum of identically zero jet polynomials, total divergences $\partial_\mu J^\mu$ with $J$ quartic, and $F(\Box-m^2)\phi$ with $F$ cubic, where $\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$. The summands may use a larger finite jet space and different engineering weights; their polynomial sum must equal $H$ before any on-shell substitution. This is an additional restriction on the selected $R_D$, not a claim about an arbitrary relation subspace or its completeness.

For $O\in U_D$ introduce commuting indeterminates $z_1,\ldots,z_4$ and complex four-vectors $k_1,\ldots,k_4$. Its polarized Fourier vertex is

$$T_O(k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4)=[z_1z_2z_3z_4]\,O\!\left(\partial_{\mu_1}\cdots\partial_{\mu_a}\phi\mapsto\sum_{j=1}^4 z_j i^a k_{j,\mu_1}\cdots k_{j,\mu_a}\right).$$

$$M_{D,N}([O])_k=\nu_0^{2k+2}\Lambda^{4-D}[v^{2k+2}]t_O(v),\qquad 0\le k\le N.$$

$$t_{O_8}(v)=8m^4+4v^2,\qquad M_{8,N}([C_8O_8])=(4\nu_0^2C_8/\Lambda^4,0,\ldots,0).$$

In particular the coefficient $[v^2]\Lambda^{-4}t_{C_8O_8}=4C_8/\Lambda^4$ is invariant under the certified relations. The target has precisely the normalized coordinate convention of the finite forward-amplitude problem. This algebraic map describes one quartic contact insertion about the free massive scalar quadratic action. It does not equate the contact polynomial to an exact full amplitude, discard loop or other-operator contributions, or infer positivity of a perturbative term from positivity of a full amplitude.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ on four-dimensional Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Let $\phi\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ be a real, Grassmann-even (commuting) scalar field of engineering dimension one, with a stable one-particle state of pole mass $m>0$; here stable means an isolated real mass pole with zero decay width. Stability and the existence of this state are physical input data; no construction of a state is asserted. An effective field theory (EFT) here is the selected local low-energy representative organized in powers of its cutoff; its exact amplitude is separate supplied model data. For the finite-jet local-operator convention, use the complexification for the finite-jet algebra and impose the usual reality condition on $\phi$. Take one field species, maximum jet order $r=1$, polynomial degree at most $q=4$, weight $D=8$, trivial internal group, and the standard Lorentz tensor action with contractions formed using $\eta$. The real operator $\mathcal O_8=(\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi)^2$ is then a local scalar of engineering dimension eight. Its coefficient in a chosen local representative is written

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EFT}}=-\frac12\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi-\frac12m^2\phi^2+\frac{C_8(\mu_*)}{\Lambda^4}\mathcal O_8+\cdots,$$

where $\Lambda>2m$ is the positive energy cutoff of the EFT description, $0<\mu_*<\Lambda$ is the chosen scale at which the coefficient and matching identity are specified, and $C_8(\mu_*)\in\mathbb R$ is dimensionless in the fixed coefficient convention and local representative. No basis-independence under field redefinitions, equations of motion, or integration by parts is asserted for $C_8$ itself.

The amplitude data consist of an identical-scalar $2\to2$ amplitude $\mathcal A(s,t,u)$ and real on-shell momenta $p_j$ with $p_j^2=-m^2$, $p_1+p_2=p_3+p_4$, and

$$s=-(p_1+p_2)^2,\qquad t=-(p_1-p_3)^2,\qquad u=-(p_1-p_4)^2,\qquad s+t+u=4m^2.$$

The forward slice is $A(s)=\mathcal A(s,0,4m^2-s)$ and assume $A(s)=A(4m^2-s)$ wherever both sides are defined. When the full $t$-dependent amplitude is supplied, use the partial-wave normalization

$$\mathcal A(s,t,u)=16\pi\sqrt{\frac{s}{s-4m^2}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}(2\ell+1)P_\ell\!\left(1+\frac{2t}{s-4m^2}\right)a_\ell(s),\qquad P_\ell(1)=1.$$

Here $\ell=0,1,2,\ldots$, $P_\ell$ is the Legendre polynomial, and $a_\ell(s)$ is the partial-wave coefficient. The formula is a normalization convention when a full amplitude is supplied; it does not assert convergence or unitarity by itself.

The $S$-matrix convention is $S=1+i(2\pi)^4\delta^4(p_{\mathrm{out}}-p_{\mathrm{in}})\mathcal A+\cdots$. The channel adopts the forward optical-theorem input $\operatorname{Im}A(s+i0)\ge0$ for $s>4m^2$ in this normalization. This sign is an assumption on the supplied amplitude data, not a deduction from the EFT truncation.

Put $\nu_0=2m^2$ and $v=s-2m^2$, so $u-2m^2=-v$. Let the specified finite list contain every isolated variable simple pole in the subthreshold interval, with real locations $p_j\in(0,4m^2)\setminus\{2m^2\}$ and real residues $r_j$. For the dimensionless amplitude convention above, $r_j$ has mass dimension two. Define the crossing-symmetric pole subtraction

$$P(s)=\sum_j\left(\frac{r_j}{s-p_j}+\frac{r_j}{4m^2-p_j-s}\right),\qquad B(v)=A(2m^2+v)-P(2m^2+v).$$

The exact amplitude data are required to be crossing even and real analytic, with $B(-v)=B(v)$, $B(\overline v)=\overline{B(v)}$, and $B$ holomorphic on

$$\Omega_{\nu_0}=\mathbb C\setminus\bigl(( -\infty,-\nu_0]\cup[\nu_0,\infty)\bigr).$$

There is no massless pole or cut at the forward point $t=0$. Require finite upper and lower cut-boundary values except at $\pm\nu_0$. Also require $B$ to extend continuously from each open half-plane onto every compact segment of either real cut bank avoiding $\pm\nu_0$. This is an extra admissibility assumption on the supplied data, not a consequence of finite pointwise boundary values or a claim about every quantum field theory. Require the uniform high-energy condition $B(w)=o(|w|^2)$ as $|w|\to\infty$ in the closed upper half-plane including upper cut-bank limits, and vanishing endpoint arcs for the cut integrals. For $\nu>\nu_0$, let $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}B(\nu+i0)$ and assign $\rho(\nu_0)=0$ by convention, without asserting a threshold boundary limit; changing this one endpoint value changes no Riemann integral; require $\rho\ge0$, local Riemann integrability on every compact subinterval of $[\nu_0,\infty)$, and finite convergence of $\int_{\nu_0}^{\infty}\rho(\nu)\nu^{-3}\,d\nu$. For every real $|v|<\nu_0$, the upper- and lower-bank integrals of $[B(x)-B(0)]/[x^2(x-v)]$ are required to exist as finite improper Riemann limits. The positive gap $m>0$ and these analytic and spectral assumptions are IR and UV input conditions; they are not derived from a finite regulator.
